_readme: MixRL tasks: which tasks train, how many prompts each adds per step, how eval is sized, and what each task is.
Edit: tasks.<name>.enabled / prompts_per_step / eval_prompts / max_response_tokens, and eval.
Training: each enabled task adds prompts_per_step prompts per step from its about.train_pool; rollout batch = their sum.
A task reshuffles and starts a new pass when its pool runs out.
Eval: each enabled task evaluates eval_prompts prompts ("all" by default, or a number up to about.val_pool) from
rl_val, eval.samples_per_prompt samples each, at baseline, every EVAL_INTERVAL steps and at the end.
Do not edit 'about' by hand: launch checks it against rl_train/rl_val and the reward service and stops on any mismatch.
about.judge: none = never calls the judge; on_miss = only when the exact check fails;
to_pass = deterministic checks can only fail an answer, passing needs the judge; always = every answer.
Reasoning inside <think>...</think> is not graded; the answer after it is. A response whose reasoning
never reaches an answer is unfinished, like a truncated one: scored 0 in training and in eval.
Training will not start if an enabled task needs the judge and the judge is unreachable, or if the reward
service cannot grade a task (for example a missing package).

math.summary: Math problems with one checkable final answer.

knowledge.summary: Factual and science questions, multiple choice and open answer.

grounding.summary: Answer only from supplied passages, without unsupported claims.

quality.summary: Open-ended assistant requests judged for helpfulness and correctness.

multiturn.summary: Keep following earlier instructions deep into a conversation.

structure.summary: Produce schema-valid JSON, YAML, TOML or CSV.

logic.summary: Puzzles and scheduling with exact answers.

python.summary: Write Python programs that pass hidden tests.

about.summary: Grade-school math word problems (openai/gsm8k) with the final answer in \boxed{}.
about.grading: math_verify checks the boxed answer against the gold number.
about.answer_format: Exactly one \boxed{...} in the answer; math_verify compares it with the gold number. Text after the box is fine; no box or two boxes fail.

about.summary: Harder competition-style math with free-form answers (nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Math-v2).
about.grading: The judge decides whether the extracted final answer is equivalent to the reference.
about.answer_format: When the prompt asks for \boxed{} (most rows) the last box goes to the judge and a response without one fails; otherwise the judge sees the whole answer after the last "Answer:"/"Final answer:" line, or the whole response.

about.summary: Multiple-choice knowledge questions with up to ten options (nvidia/Nemotron-RL-knowledge-mcqa).
about.grading: The chosen label must equal the answer key: 1.0 in the format the prompt asks for, 0.5 in the other explicit format, 0 otherwise. pass@k counts only the requested format.
about.answer_format: A final "Answer: X" line or \boxed{X}, whichever the row's prompt asks for (the other format earns half credit); the last match counts. Markdown around the letter and text after it are fine.

about.grading: The judge decides whether the boxed answer is equivalent to the reference.
about.answer_format: \boxed{...} (braces matched to any depth); only the last boxed span goes to the judge. No box fails.

about.summary: Open science questions; each prompt names its own final-answer format (nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Science-v1).
about.grading: The judge decides whether the extracted final answer is equivalent to the reference.
about.answer_format: One of nine formats named in the prompt (\boxed{}, **bold**, ((X)), Final Answer: ||X||, (Answer: X), <final_answer>, Answer is [X], <<X>>, [Answer: X]); only the last match goes to the judge, with brackets inside the answer kept. The requested format missing fails.

about.summary: Multi-hop questions answered only from supplied Wikipedia passages (hotpotqa, distractor setting).
about.grading: The judge checks the answer matches a reference alias and every claim is supported by the passages.
about.answer_format: Needs a "Final answer: <short answer>" line (markdown and "Answer:" accepted, text after it allowed); a response without one fails. The judge reads the whole response and rejects claims the passages do not support.

about.summary: General assistant requests (nvidia/Nemotron-Cascade-RL-RLHF, not list or plan prompts).
about.grading: The judge scores 1-5 against a rubric, mapped to 0-1; failing an essential check scores 0.
about.answer_format: Free form; the judge reads the whole response. Rubric: accurate, complete, obeys the request; length is neither rewarded nor penalized.

about.summary: Assistant requests that ask for a list or enumeration (nvidia/Nemotron-Cascade-RL-RLHF).
about.grading: The judge scores 1-5 against a rubric, mapped to 0-1; failing an essential check scores 0.
about.answer_format: Free form; the judge reads the whole response. Rubric also rejects repeated list items.

about.summary: Assistant requests that ask for a plan, itinerary or schedule (nvidia/Nemotron-Cascade-RL-RLHF).
about.grading: The judge scores 1-5 against a rubric, mapped to 0-1; failing an essential check scores 0.
about.answer_format: Free form; the judge reads the whole response. Rubric: accurate, complete, obeys the request.

about.summary: Final turn of a multi-turn chat that tests memory of earlier instructions (Nemotron-RL-Multichallenge, vanilla).
about.grading: The judge answers each rubric check against the completed conversation, the response as its final turn; every check must pass.
about.answer_format: Free form; each rubric check is judged against the whole response.
requires: judge: up to 2 calls per answer
judge context of at least 32K tokens (JUDGE_CONTEXT)

about.summary: Harder multi-turn chats with system personas and longer histories (Nemotron-RL-Multichallenge, advanced).
about.grading: The judge answers each rubric check against the completed conversation, the response as its final turn; every check must pass.
about.answer_format: Free form; each rubric check is judged against the whole response.
requires: judge: up to 6 calls per answer
judge context of at least 32K tokens (JUDGE_CONTEXT)

about.summary: Requests with verifiable format constraints such as case, length or punctuation (nvidia/Nemotron-RL-instruction_following).
about.grading: IFBench checkers test each constraint; all must pass.
about.answer_format: Free form, but every listed constraint (length, case, keywords, layout) is checked on the whole response.
requires: ifbench with nltk, spacy, langdetect, emoji, syllapy and immutabledict in the reward service

about.summary: Produce JSON, YAML, TOML or CSV that matches a given schema (Nemotron-RL-Instruction-Following-Structured-Outputs-v2).
about.grading: Data that parses and matches the schema goes to the judge, which must confirm the content; CSV cells are converted to the schema's types.
about.answer_format: Valid JSON/YAML/TOML/CSV for the schema, alone or inside explanation (a fenced block, or an embedded JSON value); the last one given counts and must match the schema. Rows whose schema no document can satisfy are excluded.
requires: pyyaml, jsonschema and defusedxml in the reward service
judge context of at least 32K tokens (JUDGE_CONTEXT)

about.grading: Exact match on the final answer; the judge re-checks only answers that miss.
about.answer_format: Exact match on the last "Answer:"/"Final answer:" line, or on the whole response if there is none; misses go to the judge.
requires: judge (only for answers that miss the exact match)

about.summary: Multi-turn scheduling: return a JSON calendar that satisfies every time constraint (Nemotron-RL-Instruction-Following-Calendar-v2).
about.grading: A deterministic checker validates the final calendar against every constraint.
about.answer_format: The final calendar as a JSON list, alone or inside explanation; the last JSON value given counts.

about.summary: Competitive programming problems solved in Python (codeparrot/apps).
about.grading: The last Python code block runs against the problem's tests in a Docker sandbox; needs the APPS audit (MIXRL_CODE_AUDIT_DIR).
about.answer_format: A python code block is required (no block fails); the last block that reads stdin runs, so usage-example blocks are fine. stdout must match the tests token by token.
requires: Docker CLI and the sandbox image suryavikram6/chimera-eval:0.1.1 visible to the reward service
